quotes.quote: Here we ran a six-month randomized control trial investigating the effects of hybrid working from home on 1,612 employees in a Chinese technology company in 2021–2022. We found that hybrid working improved job satisfaction and reduced quit rates by one-third. The reduction in quit rates was significant for non-managers, female employees and those with long commutes. Null equivalence tests showed that hybrid working did not affect performance grades over the next two years of reviews.
quotes.location: Nature 630, open-access full text on nature.com, abstract

quotes.quote: Trip.com decided to evaluate the effects of hybrid WFH on the 1,612 engineering, marketing and finance employees in the Airfare and IT divisions, spanning 395 managers and 1,217 non-managers.

quotes.quote: Employees were randomized by even or odd birthdays into the option to WFH on Wednesday and Friday and come into the office on the other three days, or to come into the office on all five days.
